product_one_liner.value: Owl provides insurers with an AI claims platform that reads claim-file documents, signals and records and turns them into structured, cited evidence for claims teams to act on.

pricing_page.notes: The homepage navigation and footer have no pricing link, and the /pricing route did not yield a page.

named_customers.notes: The success-story case studies identify customers only generically (for example, a multiline insurer), not by name.

founded_year.notes: The company funding announcement and PitchBook say 2018; a LinkedIn excerpt separately says 2019.

eng_blog.notes: The resource index shows insurance/product and industry-focused content, not an engineering blog about how the product is built.

public_docs.notes: The public docs site has multiple categories and task-oriented guides.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The open-role list includes engineering and product jobs, but none has an AI/ML or data-science title.

model_provider.value: Owl’s custom vision-language model; its documentation names Owl-1.5 among its model cards.
model_provider.notes: The public sources do not identify a third-party production inference provider.

compliance_certs.notes: The Trust Center lists GDPR under Compliance; the security page names SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and HIPAA. PCI DSS is not named.

raised_18mo.notes: The latest identified round was the November 2021 Series B, before the 18-month window ending 2026-11-09.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The careers page lists an Enterprise Account Executive role.

launched_6mo.notes: On May 9, 2026, Owl described Template Assistant as a new feature.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The current executive roster is small and lists no recent C-level or VP start; no departure announcement was found.
